items.text: Social norms are so pervasive and so deeply embedded in our performative muscle memory that we typically engage in them without even thinking. <break time="0.8s" /> When someone greets us and asks, How are you, we tend to respond automatically with something along the lines of I am OK or Not bad. <break time="0.8s" /> The response is hardly ever You know, I am having a pretty awful day, and I am really worried because there is talk of layoffs happening at my job, even though that may be the case. <break time="0.8s" /> This degree of transparency upon greeting someone is typically perceived as socially awkward. <break time="0.8s" /> The list of social norms within a given community or society is ever growing and ever changing as community members negotiate what is acceptable behavior based on the standing beliefs and ideologies of the collective. <break time="0.8s" /> During this process, new rules are constructed and enforced to establish expectations for community members. <break time="0.8s" /> Social norms could easily be reduced to practicing good behavior, but it is much more than that. <break time="0.8s" /> Social norms are the means by which social cohesion is achieved. <break time="0.8s" /> And we navigate these rules, and thousands more like them, every single day.
